# mmx-ran-1.3 — a Hobbit Ranger on seed 137, and what the level really costs

**40 asks of its own (265 to 304) and 155 in the whole life, depth 1,
character level 2, 366 gold, wealth 931, alive and at full hit points.** No
down staircase was ever seen, on either level this character was on. What the
life did buy is a set of measurements that change how the next Ranger should
spend its asks — and a correction of what my own last life told me.

| | |
|---|---|
| seed | 137 |
| character | Hobbit Ranger "Runner", age 27, STR 15, INT 12, WIS 16, DEX 18/20, CON 14 |
| stats | Cur AC 10 (2 naked, +8 from the Soft Leather Armour), HP 17/17 |
| depth | 1 — the deepest level reached, on two different depth-1 levels |
| turns | 12277 |
| experience | 10, which is character level 2 |
| gold | 366 (126 inherited, 180 found on the floor, 84 spent on the armour) |
| wealth | 931 |
| coverage | **294 of the 1716 box tiles of the whole-level map, 17 %** — and no `>` on any of them |
| outcome | stopped, alive, at full hit points |
| own tools | none (I used the shared `tools/screen/` ones and the game's own commands) |

## The three findings that change how to play

### 1. The town costs one tile per ask, and the Recall is the way out of it

`cmd-pickup.c`'s `do_autopickup()` calls `disturb(p)` for **every object on
the square you step onto**, and `disturb()` signals `EVENT_INPUT_FLUSH`, which
this build's patch turns into "drop the rest of the key string". The town's
floor carries goods the map does not draw, so in the town:

| method | tiles per ask, in the town |
|---|---|
| digit chain of 20 keys | **1** |
| look-mode aimed walk (`l p <digits> g`) | 1–2 |
| run (`.` + direction) | 2 |
| the same chain in the dungeon | 5–24 |

The shop is 12 to 33 tiles from the town's staircase, so a shopping trip as
the manuals imagine it costs 20 to 60 asks. **Mine cost thirty.**

The way out is the Scroll of Word of Recall. `effect_handler_RECALL` sets
`player->word_recall = randint0(20) + 15`; `game-world.c` decrements it once
per player action; and when it reaches zero **in the town** it calls
`dungeon_change_level(player, player->recall_depth)`, where `recall_depth` is
`MAX(recall_depth, 1)` — the deepest level you have reached. So:

```
read the Recall (1 ask), then R + backspace + 60 + Enter (1 ask)
```

and the Recall fires during the rest and puts you on depth 1. **Two asks
instead of nineteen.** It costs the scroll, which is the escape you wanted
to keep, so spend it on a trip you are sure of.

### 2. The aimed walk is not a sweep, and my own last life was wrong about it

My previous life reported `*` + `p` + digits + `g` as "9–23 actions, the
fastest move in the game" and recommended it as the main sweep tool. I
measured it forty times on this level:

| aimed walk | 0 | 1 | 2 | 9 | 12 | 13 | 16 | 20 | 21 | 22 | 23 | 27 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| actions | 6 | 11 | 9 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 1 |

**Median 2.** The reason is in the source: `find_path` treats an unknown
destination as passable, so the path it builds is a straight line through
ground it has not looked at, and the walk then stops at the **first real
wall**. The aim barely matters; the local geometry does. A digit chain of
20–24 keys in one direction, or the game's own `lxg`, covers the same ground
five to ten times faster.

### 3. A Ranger's right target on depth 1 is a grey mould, and her wrong one is a giant ant

`monster.txt`, measured:

| monster | hp | AC | exp at CL1 | damage | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **grey mould** | 2 | 1 | 3 | 1d4 | never moves; its spore only HURTS |
| **wild dog** | 3 | 3 | 1 | 1d1 | flees in terror when hit |
| white worm mass | 10 | 1 | 2 | 1d2 + poison | **multiplies** when hit |
| giant white mouse | 2 | 4 | 1 | 1d2 | multiplies |
| giant black ant | 11 | 24 | 3 | 1d2 | **unkillable for this character** |
| small kobold | 8 | 24 | 5 | 1d5 | **unkillable for this character** |
| floating eye | 11 | 7 | 1 | gaze:paralyse | never moves; shoot it from range |

The grey mould is the best target in the game for a Ranger with a bow:
armour class 1, two hit points, three experience, and it cannot reach me. The
grey **mushroom patch** (glyph `,`) is a different animal — its spore
*confuses* — and the yellow one *terrifies*.

The armoured monsters are the trap. The bow's to-hit of 32 against AC 24 is
53 per cent and the oil's to-hit of 11 is on the flat 12 per cent floor, so
against a giant black ant both are a coin flip at best, the melee is worse,
and the ant's 1d2 is not what kills me — the eleven of its hit points are.

**And the arrow does 1d4, not 1d4 × 2.** My own `RANGER.md` said the Short
Bow's pval of 2 doubles the arrow. It does not: the message says
"Your Arrow (1d4)", the floating eye lost 8 hit points to two arrows, and
the two-hit-point grey mould needed **two** arrows, so the first did one
point of damage. `player-calcs.c` sets `state->ammo_mult = launcher->pval`
and `player-attack.c` multiplies by it, and neither happened. One arrow is
1 to 4 damage, average 2.5; one arrow kills a two-hit-point mouse 75 per
cent of the time.

## The level, and why the staircase was not found

A depth-1 level is 198 × 66 squares with **three or four** down staircases
(`gen-cave.c`: `handle_level_stairs(..., rand_range(3, 4), ...)`), each at
least 16 tiles from the others and from the up staircase, and each on a
square with **exactly three adjacent walls** — that is, at the end of a
corridor.

The whole-level map is the only honest picture of it: `display_map`
(`ui-map.c`) computes `row = (y * map_hgt) / cave->height` for every square,
so the 78 × 22 box is the whole level scaled, and `explore.py` counts it.
I pressed `M` every ten to fifteen asks and read it each time:

| | |
|---|---|
| box tiles with terrain | 294 of 1716 — **17 % of the level** |
| down staircases seen | **none** |
| where the dark was | north-east at first, then south-west, then south-east |
| where I was | from the western middle (x ≈ 43, y ≈ 33) to the north-east corner (x ≈ 175, y ≈ 9) |

Seventeen per cent with three or four staircases on the level is entirely
consistent with finding none: the expected number of staircases inside 17 %
of the level is 0.6. **The number that would settle it is the coverage at the
moment a `>` first appears**, and that is what the next run should report.

Two things made the sweep slower than it should have been:

- **The remembered map lies.** It drew floor at squares that were walls
  ((45,12), (23,15), (44,12)), and a chain that trusted it died with "There
  is a wall in the way!" and an empty message line. Read the ground with
  `tools/screen/look.py`, which gives every drawn glyph as an offset from
  `@`.
- **An awake monster cuts every chain.** A wild dog bit me and the chain
  stopped after one tile; the two white worm masses were worse, because they
  **multiply when hit** — I shot one and a second appeared. A breeding
  monster in a room is a tax on every ask, not only on its own.

## What else I measured

- **A teleport trap is on depth 1 and it is a way across the level.** One
  fired me from the western middle to the far north-east corner in one step,
  for no damage. But there is **no trap door on depth 1**: `trap.txt` gives
  the trap door `appear:1:2:0` — rarity 1, **min_depth 2** — so the trap
  door is not a way down here. The depth-1 traps are the teleport, the pit,
  the confusion and the slow ones (`gen-cave.c` `try_door` puts a trap on a
  junction square with probability `tun.jct / 500`).
- **`lxg` is the game's own explorer and it can walk a long way**: 23 tiles
  in one ask at ask 274, and it never fails, because the square it aims at is
  beside ground you have already seen. When the frontier is right next to
  you it walks one tile, so it is a frontier crawl; the digit chain is the
  sweep.
- **The experience economy of depth 1 ends at level 2.** A kill pays
  `(mexp × monster level) / character level`, so at level 2 a wild dog's 1
  experience becomes 0 and a grey mould's 3 becomes 1. Level 3 needs 18 more
  experience on depth 1 and is out of reach; at depth 2 every kill doubles.
  **That is the whole argument for finding the staircase.**
- **The M map's scale is 3 level tiles to a box row and 2.5 to a box column**,
  so the dark direction it reports is a real direction, and the panel's own
  coordinates scroll in jumps of 33 columns — read positions from the library,
  not from the panel.
- **A server restart kills the game, and the run survives it.** `borg_runner
  carry-on --run runs/<run>` replays the run's own keys into a fresh run of
  the next generation and reports `identical: true`; the character, the
  gold, the armour class and the level came back exactly. That is what
  `mmx-ran-1.2` → `mmx-ran-1.3` is.

## What I could not see or do

- 83 % of a depth-1 level, and no down staircase.
- I never used the Scroll of Phase Door (a way out), the Cure Light Wounds
  (I was never hurt enough) or the Scroll of Word of Recall (I spent it on
  the town, which was the right call).
- I did not read either unknown consumable I found (a Magenta Potion and a
  scroll titled "ma adio malum"). On depth 1 a scroll is 7 % a Deep Descent,
  which drops me five levels below my deepest, and 3 % a Summon Monster; at
  character level 2 the first use of an unknown scroll is worth 1 experience
  at most, which cannot reach level 3. **Both were worth more carried than
  used.**
- I never read the shop's 's' (give) trick to identify an unknown kind,
  because I had no shop to give it to after the town.

## Leads, with what would settle each

1. **How much of a depth-1 level does a run have to cover to find a
   staircase?** *Settled by:* a run that reports the M map's coverage at the
   moment the first `>` appears. This run's 17 % with none is the other half
   of the number.
2. **Is the Recall a reliable way down from the town?** *Settled by:* a run
   that reads it in the town, rests, and reports the depth it lands on. Mine
   landed on depth 1 with 26 player actions of a 15–34 timer.
3. **What is a depth-1 level's room count, and how many of its corridors end
   in a dead end?** *Settled by:* counting the dead ends on one level's whole
   map. If there are forty and three of them are staircases, a sweep that
   visits dead ends is the sweep.
4. **Which monster gives the most experience per arrow on depth 1?** *Settled
   by:* counting arrows per kill by race, the way `mmx-war-1` counted arrows.
   The grey mould is two arrows for 3 experience; a mouse is 1–2 arrows for 1.
5. **What is on the level's other side?** *Settled by:* a run that carries the
   town trip in its first ten asks, so that it has 140 asks left for the level
   instead of 110 — and a run that reaches depth 2 while it still has
   arrows.

## The report I would write if I had it

Buy the Soft Leather Armour in the first ten asks and read the Recall in the
town: that is twenty asks spent, and it buys a character who can survive
depth 2 and a way back into it. Then sweep with digit chains, watch the M
map every ten asks, kill grey moulds and wild dogs with the bow whenever one
is near, and remember that on depth 1 the experience ends at level 2 — so
**the staircase is the whole game**, and the sweep should follow corridors
to their ends rather than cover area.
